DocumentationNarrative.Body: Command-line tools for BI modeling, conversion, validation, and execution.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: CLI

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Model references for the sanctioned BI metadata workspaces.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A BI stack can begin with a source schema, pass through Raw and Business Data Vault structures, continue into a dimensional warehouse, and finish in an analytical target. At each handoff, the next workspace receives declared structure and the evidence needed to bind, generate, deploy, or execute it.
The result is a chain that can be inspected at every boundary instead of one opaque build script.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: How the layers connect

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The AdventureWorks stack composes 27 workspaces and 29 named operations over a live `AdventureWorks2022` source:
- source schema synchronization; - Raw and Business Data Vault and dimensional warehouse creation and deployment; - 53 source-to-Raw, 47 Raw-to-Business, and 20 Business-to-warehouse transforms imported and strictly bound; - three pipelines with modeled cross-pipeline orchestration; - 176 generated Data Quality checks; - portable `MetaAnalytics` projected into `MetaTabular`, then deployed and processed.
A clean run reconciled 31,465 orders, 121,317 order lines, and 163 quota rows from source through the warehouse. It reproduced the expected sales and quota totals and produced zero findings across the promoted Data Quality checks. Repeating the ETL preserved the Raw, Business, and warehouse row totals, and the processed Tabular deployment returned the same analytical values.
Once the stack is created and deployed:
```powershell cd Demos\AdventureWorksBiStackDemo\AdventureWorksBiStackDemo.MetaMesh meta-mesh run --operation run-etl meta-mesh run --operation verify-stack meta-mesh run --operation deploy-tabular meta-mesh run --operation process-tabular ```
The operation names and workspace dependencies are part of the MetaMesh workspace, so the sequence can be inspected and repeated from the model.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: AdventureWorks evidence

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The official BI models divide the stack by ownership:
- `MetaSchema`, `MetaDataType`, and `MetaDataTypeConversion` describe source structures and type mappings. - `MetaRawDataVault`, `MetaBusinessDataVault`, and `MetaDataWarehouse` describe data architecture and physical implementation. - `MetaTransformScript`, `MetaTransformBinding`, `MetaSql`, and `MetaSqlDeployManifest` describe transformation, binding, database objects, and deployment. - `MetaAnalytics` carries portable analytical meaning before a target engine is selected. - `MetaTabular` and `MetaMultiDimensional` describe target-specific analytical models. - `MetaDataQuality`, `MetaPipeline`, and `MetaOrchestration` describe assurance and execution.
`meta-convert` connects these workspaces through explicit model conversions.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: BI model layers

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta-data-quality` turns transform and schema information into generated quality checks and findings.
`meta-pipeline` executes modeled tasks and records the transform, binding, row, batch, timeout, fingerprint, audit, and failure information needed to understand a run. `meta-orchestration` derives dependencies from pipeline tasks and modeled object access, while explicit ordering, synchronization, and failure policy remain part of the orchestration workspace.
Target CLIs deploy or process the analytical workspaces described by the stack.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Execution models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
SQL structure matters to the BI layers that depend on it.
`MetaTransformScript` imports supported SQL into a typed syntax model and can emit equivalent SQL. `MetaTransformBinding` checks that modeled reads and writes resolve against source and target `MetaSchema` workspaces and follow the selected `MetaDataTypeConversion` policy. `MetaSql` and `MetaSqlDeployManifest` carry deployable database structure and controlled deployment.
The result is a chain of declared contracts rather than independent tools guessing from SQL text.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: SQL structure and binding

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta-bi` is the BI modeling layer built on `meta`. It carries source contracts through SQL transformation, Data Vault, warehouse, quality, pipeline, orchestration, and analytical target workspaces. Each handoff remains a workspace that can be reviewed, converted, deployed, or executed.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Overview

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Command-line tools for the core metadata foundation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: CLI

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Model references for the core metadata foundation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta` is organized around the work done on a workspace:
- **Create:** make an empty workspace or create one surface from another. - **Inspect:** view workspace state, models, instances, relationships, and graphs. - **Author:** add and change model definitions and instance records. - **Refactor:** change model structure together with the affected instance data. - **Import and export:** bring in external metadata and write the selected workspace surface.
Use `meta help` for the current command surface and command-specific options.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: The meta command surface

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Workspace-oriented commands operate on the current working directory by default. Use `--workspace <path>` to target another workspace.
Use `meta help` for the available commands and `meta help <command>` for the options and arguments of one command. The command reference below is generated from the same command surface used by the CLI.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Command guide

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A C# workspace is readable and writable typed source for the same model and instance graph. Create it from an existing workspace when an application or service should work with the workspace in C#:
```powershell meta create --new-workspace .\CSharpWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --csharp ```
The result is a workspace surface, not a separate tooling product.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: C# workspace creation

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Create an empty XML workspace, then create SQL and C# workspaces from it:
```powershell meta create --new-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --xml
$env:META_SQL_CONNECTION = "Server=.;Database=WorkspaceCatalog;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" meta create --new-workspace .\SqlWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --connection-env META_SQL_CONNECTION --sql meta create --new-workspace .\CSharpWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --csharp ```
All three workspaces carry the same declared model and instance graph.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Create a workspace on a selected surface

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The `meta create` command copies a model, and optionally its instances, into a new workspace surface. The source and destination are explicit, so the operation is repeatable and easy to inspect:
```powershell meta create --new-workspace .\SqlWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --connection-env META_SQL_CONNECTION --sql meta create --new-workspace .\CSharpWorkspace --source-workspace .\SqlWorkspace --with-instances --csharp ```
The selected surface owns storage and execution. The workspace semantics remain unchanged.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Change a workspace surface

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Metadata is the structure that tools operate on. A model defines entity types, scalar properties, and relationships. Its instance graph contains identified records and references. A workspace carries both so the same declared meaning can be authored, inspected, changed, and moved between surfaces.
Core terms:
- **Model:** a named set of entity definitions. - **Entity:** a record type with an identity. - **Property:** a scalar value on an entity. - **Relationship:** a reference from one entity to another. - **Instance:** one identified record of an entity. - **Workspace:** the unit that carries a model, its instance graph, and the selected surface.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Metadata foundations

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Build the foundation from the repository root:
```powershell dotnet build Metadata.Framework.sln ```
Run the CLI directly during development:
```powershell dotnet run --project Meta\Cli\Meta.Cli.csproj -- help ```
The installer can publish the foundation CLIs for a machine with the .NET 8 runtime. The repository build and the published executables use the same modeled command surfaces.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Development and installation

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`instances/*.xml` stores the records for an XML workspace. The root element names the model, and each entity is grouped under its deterministic list container.
For the small fictional `WorkspaceCatalog` model:
```xml <WorkspaceCatalog> <SystemList> <System Id="erp"> <SystemName>ERP</SystemName> </System> </SystemList> </WorkspaceCatalog> ```
Every record has an `Id`. Scalar properties are child elements; relationships are stored as `...Id` attributes. Missing elements mean that an optional value is unset.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: XML instance contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The foundation package boundary is explicit:
- `Meta.Operations` owns representation-neutral state, reads, constraints, and operations. - `Meta.Core` owns shared model algorithms and deterministic core behavior. - `Meta.Surfaces` owns XML, SQL, and C# workspace surfaces. - `Meta.Integration` owns import, export, deployment, and service composition. - `MetaWeave.Core` owns the MetaWeave domain library.
`pack-internal.cmd` packs these internal packages in dependency order for downstream CLI development.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Foundation package boundary

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A workspace has one semantic content and several first-class surfaces. XML, SQL, and C# can carry the same model and instance graph without changing its meaning. Changing the surface changes how the workspace is stored and operated on; it does not change the entities, properties, relationships, or records.
Commands work through the selected surface. XML is a deterministic file surface, SQL is a database surface, and C# is a typed source surface.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Surface-agnostic workspaces

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`model.xml` declares the schema for an XML workspace: which entities exist, which scalar properties they carry, and how they relate.
A model has one `<Model name="WorkspaceCatalog">` root and follows a small set of rules:
- `<Entity name="System">` defines a record type; every entity has an implicit `Id`. - `<PropertyList>` contains scalar fields. Properties are required by default; `isRequired="false"` makes one optional. - `<RelationshipList>` contains references to other entities. Relationships are required by default. - A relationship role distinguishes multiple relationships to the same target entity. - Entity instances are grouped under deterministic `<EntityName>List` containers.
The XML model contract keeps structure explicit and reviewable.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: XML model contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The foundation is delivered through five command-line tools:
- **`meta`** creates and operates on model and instance workspaces across XML, SQL, and C# surfaces. - **`meta-cli`** defines command surfaces and provides shared parsing, help, workspace access, and runtime binding. - **`meta-weave`** defines and validates sanctioned property bindings across models, then materializes those bindings when a combined workspace is needed. - **`meta-docs`** combines CLI and model reference data with authored technical documentation, then merges and renders the public reference. - **`meta-mesh`** declares the workspaces involved in a repository workflow and the ordered executable steps that operate on them.
BI-specific models and command-line tools live in the separate `meta-bi` repository.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Foundation command-line tools

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A SQL workspace is a database carrying the model and instance graph. Create one from an existing workspace by supplying the connection environment variable required for the target database:
```powershell $env:META_SQL_CONNECTION = "Server=.;Database=WorkspaceCatalog;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" meta create --new-workspace .\SqlWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --connection-env META_SQL_CONNECTION --sql ```
SQL operations then work against the database surface instead of first turning the database into an XML file.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: SQL workspace creation

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta` is the foundation for model-first metadata. It creates and operates on workspaces that carry a model and its instance graph across XML, SQL, and C# surfaces.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Overview

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The XML surface fits naturally into Git. Model definitions, instance data, and refactors remain structured, so changes can be reviewed as metadata rather than as an opaque file rewrite. Stable ordering and consistent encoding keep diffs focused on the change itself.
Teams that work primarily in SQL or C# can use those surfaces directly and still move the same workspace through the foundation tools.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: XML surface and version control

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A workspace contains a model, its instance graph, and the storage owned by its selected surface.
The line-oriented `workspace.meta` descriptor identifies the selected surface. It records `representation xml`, `representation csharp`, or `representation sql`; a SQL workspace also records the environment variable that locates its database. The surface owns its layout and persistence details, while the workspace contents remain the same model and instance graph.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Workspace contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Each surface fits a different working style while carrying the same workspace semantics:
- **XML** keeps model and instance files deterministic, reviewable, and easy to version in Git. - **SQL** keeps metadata in a database, with relational integrity, queries, and set-based changes available where the data lives. - **C#** keeps the workspace as readable and writable typed source for applications and services.
The choice is operational. It does not create a second meaning for the model.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: XML, SQL, and C# surfaces
